title: Project Context Document (PCD)
description: The canonical, typed data structure for a single hackathon project. One PCD per project. Every read and write goes through this schema. Render layer (JSON-to-Markdown) consumes this; canonical store IS this.

schema_version.description: PCD schema version. Used for migration when the schema evolves.

project_id.description: ULID. Stable identifier used for cross-references and Vault links.

project_name.description: Human-readable name. Defaults to the hackathon name.

archived_at.description: Null while the project is active. Set when archived (post-Phase 7 or manually). Archived projects are read-only; reopening clears this field.

current_phase.description: Active phase number. Phase 0 is Vault-level, not project-level.

phase_4_gate_crossed.description: Once true, never returns to false. Backward navigation past Phase 4 is forbidden. Scope changes go through the Addendum Protocol.

vault_references.description: References (by ID) to Vault entries that informed this project. Populated as queries are made during phases. Stores IDs only — entry contents are not duplicated into the PCD.

sections.description: All content sections, each with shared metadata via the SectionEnvelope pattern. Order here is canonical render order.

phase_gate_log.description: Append-only log of phase completions, overrides, addenda, and reconciliation actions. Forms the auditable history of the project.

addenda.description: TID Addenda created via the Addendum Protocol. Original TID is never edited; addenda are appended.

SectionEnvelope.description: Metadata wrapper present on every section. Content lives in `data`. Staleness, dependencies, and provenance are tracked here.

data.description: Section-specific content. Schema is defined per Section_* type.

is_populated.description: False when the section has not yet been filled by its phase. Distinct from being empty — a populated section may legitimately have empty subfields.

is_stale.description: True when an upstream dependency was modified after this section was populated. Cleared by Regenerate, Confirm-as-valid, or Manual-edit reconciliation.

stale_reason.description: Human-readable explanation. E.g. 'problem_analysis was updated on 2026-04-27 14:32; this section was derived from the previous version.'

extraction_confidence.description: Self-reported confidence from the Flash extractor for the most recent intake. Null for manually-edited sections.

user_overrides.description: Audit trail of manual edits made after extraction. Useful for debugging extraction quality.

user_justification.description: Required for override events. Optional otherwise.
Required. Why this scope change is necessary.

content_markdown.description: The addendum body itself: what changes, what it impacts, revised do-not-build list.

build_state_snapshot.description: Pasted Cursor build-state markdown the addendum was authored against. Preserved for audit.

problem_statement_raw.description: Verbatim problem statement as released by organizers. Never edited.

judging_criteria_raw.description: Verbatim judging criteria as released. May be null at Phase 1 if not yet announced.

flagged_unknowns.description: Things the user knows are unresolved and must monitor (e.g. 'judges not yet announced').

judge_personas.description: Composite profiles of likely judges. May be inferred from organizer/sponsor signals when judges are not yet announced.

is_inferred.description: True if no specific judge name is associated; persona is built from proxy signals.

vault_judge_id.description: ID into the Judge & Organizer Database if this judge is on file.

values.description: What this persona is likely to value in a solution.

skepticisms.description: What this persona is likely to be skeptical of.

memorable_solution_patterns.description: What kinds of solutions have impressed similar judges historically.

past_winner_patterns.description: What has won past hackathons run by this organizer or in this domain.

criteria_drift_warnings.description: Flags raised by the system about ways the active rubric may shift based on the organizer profile.

weight.description: Fractional weight. All criteria weights must sum to 1.0.

judge_questions.description: The questions a judge in this category typically asks themselves.

unmapped_official_criteria.description: Official criteria fragments that didn't map cleanly onto the rubric schema. Flagged for user interpretation.

team_framing.description: The team's own framing of the problem. May differ from organizer's verbatim language.

five_whys_chain.description: Sequential root-cause chain. Each entry is one 'why?' deeper than the last.

hmw_reframes.description: How-Might-We reframes, prioritized to non-obvious angles.

differentiation_angles.description: Top 2-3 angles where differentiation is possible. Cross-referenced with competitive_landscape.

premortem_completed.description: Hard requirement for Phase 2 completion. Cannot be bypassed without Phase Gate Log override.

predicted_average_solutions.description: The 3-5 solutions most teams will converge on. Map of the crowded space.

spaces_to_avoid.description: Explicit no-go directions extracted from the predicted average solutions.

differentiation_seams.description: Positive-direction counterpart to spaces_to_avoid. Gaps between predicted-average archetypes — unmet stakeholders, missing dimensions, ignored constraints — where differentiation oxygen exists. Notes for the team to ideate against in Phase 3, not solutions themselves.

research_status.description: Tracks whether real user research happened. 'skipped_no_user_access' is the legitimate fallback when target users are unreachable.

is_inferred.description: True if persona is inferred from the brief rather than from real user contact.

psychographics.description: Personality traits and core values. Optional; populated by the user research package prompt's expanded persona schema. Personality traits and values are kept separate by design — they describe different things.

values.description: 3-5 things this persona ranks above other things, e.g. 'autonomy', 'family stability', 'professional reputation'.

technology_behavior.description: How this persona interacts with technology in everyday life. Optional. Used by Phase 3 ideation prompts to ground feature design in real platform habits, not assumed ones.

platforms_used.description: Specific named apps, sites, or channels this persona uses regularly. 'Messenger', 'TikTok', 'GCash' — not 'social media' or 'banking apps'.

usage_patterns.description: When, how often, and what for. e.g. 'checks Messenger continuously during work hours; opens banking app only on payday'.

sources_of_influence.description: 3-5 specific influence vectors this persona trusts when forming opinions or making decisions. Specific named individuals, institutions, communities, media outlets, or peer groups — not generic categories like 'friends' or 'social media'.

validates_assumption.description: Free-text assumption being validated, OR a hypothesis id from research_hypotheses[].id (e.g. 'hyp_01HXY...'). The render layer detects the id pattern and links to the hypothesis.

challenges_assumption.description: Free-text assumption being challenged, OR a hypothesis id from research_hypotheses[].id. Same id-detection rule as validates_assumption.

research_hypotheses.description: Falsifiable beliefs the team holds about the problem space, produced by the phase_2_research_hypotheses prompt. Each hypothesis is testable by user research; interview_insights[].validates_assumption / .challenges_assumption may reference these by id.

id.description: ULID-prefixed identifier, e.g. 'hyp_01HXY...'. Used as the cross-reference target from interview_insights.

category.description: 1:1 mapping from the prompt's five headings. Sort to canonical category order on render.

statement.description: Single-sentence falsifiable assertion. Names a specific population, behavior, or mechanism.

falsification_signal.description: Optional: what evidence would disprove this hypothesis. Populated by the user during research planning, not by the LLM.

status.description: Updated as interview_insights accumulate. The render layer derives a status proposal from referenced insights, but the canonical value is set by the user.

calibrated_experts.description: The calibrated identities of the domain expert and technical expert used to seed the SCAMPER dialogue, derived from hackathon_profile.organizer_type and theme. Auditable provenance for the SCAMPER output — lets the user verify the lens was correct for this hackathon. Optional; populated when the LLM emits the required calibrated-experts header.

domain_expert.description: e.g. 'bank executive (risk & compliance lens)' or 'public-sector clinician (care continuity lens)'.

technical_expert.description: e.g. 'fintech engineer (core-banking integration lens)' or 'interoperability engineer (HL7/FHIR lens)'.

scored_shortlist.description: Ideas scored against the active rubric by the Downselection Prompt.

team_idea_seed.description: Output of the optional Step 3a Idea Seed Challenge. Populated only when the user supplied a preconceived idea and ran it through the Grill-Me interrogation. Null when Step 3a was skipped.

original_text.description: The user's preconceived idea, verbatim, as entered before the Idea Seed Challenge.

challenge_outcome.description: Verdict from the Grill-Me dialogue. 'adopt_as_seed' = use the seed unchanged; 'refined' = use the seed with the refinement captured in refined_text; 'rejected' = do not carry the seed forward.

refined_text.description: The refined idea text. Required when challenge_outcome === 'refined'; null otherwise.

verdict_rationale.description: Resolved Summary rationale from the Grill-Me dialogue. Explains why the seed was adopted, refined, or rejected.

candidate_portfolio.description: Output of Step 3e Divergent Candidate Generation. The 3-5 candidate ideas synthesized from the upstream ideation pipeline (SCAMPER, JTBD, Brainwriting). Null until Step 3e has been completed.

id.description: ULID. Stable identifier; referenced from chosen_direction.data.selected_candidate_id when this candidate is chosen as the final direction.

description.description: One-line description of the candidate idea.

innovation_score.description: 1-5 scale, calibrated against the active rubric's Innovation criterion.

impact_score.description: 1-5 scale, calibrated against the active rubric's Problem-Solution Fit criterion.

feasibility_score.description: 1-5 scale, calibrated against the active rubric's Feasibility & Viability criterion.

distinguishing_factors.description: Why this candidate is structurally different from the others — and from the predicted-average solutions in competitive_landscape.

archetype.description: Enforced Diversity Archetype label. 'unassigned' is used when archetypes_enforced was false at generation time.

is_remix.description: True when this candidate was produced by the in-app candidate-review remix UI rather than emitted directly by the LLM.

remix_source_ids.description: When is_remix is true, the ids of the candidates that were combined to produce this remix. Empty array otherwise.

archetypes_enforced.description: Mirrors the Step 3e Enforced Diversity Archetypes toggle state at generation time. Captured for audit so the Phase 7 debrief can correlate diversity-on vs diversity-off runs against outcomes. Default true. NOTE: This default is informational. The application sets the field explicitly to true at fresh-PCD initialization (see spec §2.6) — Ajv runs without `useDefaults: true` because applying schema defaults at validation time would mask genuinely-missing fields elsewhere in the PCD.

user_rationale.description: User's stated reasoning for the selection. Required.

user_acknowledged_overlap.description: True only if overlap_detected was true and the user explicitly chose to proceed anyway.

selected_candidate_id.description: Optional. When non-null, references CandidateIdea.id from ideation_record.data.candidate_portfolio.candidates[]; the PCD Viewer resolves this id at render time to show provenance ('Selected: Candidate X — Weird Gem archetype'). Null when the chosen direction was authored manually rather than selected from the portfolio.

mvp_definition.description: One-paragraph definition of the minimum viable demonstrable build.

vault_boilerplate_id.description: Reference to a Boilerplate Library entry that fulfills this component.

data.description: Shape Up format. Human-readable; for judges, mentors, teammates.

appetite.description: What the team commits to building within available time.

data.description: Technical Implementation Document. Exhaustive; for Cursor and CLI tools.

screens.description: Screen-by-screen breakdown. The single most important field for productive AI coding.

core_user_flow.description: Shortest path that proves the solution works.

data.description: Lightweight strategic skeleton — bullet points, not narrative. Teammates write the actual deck.

visuals_slides.description: Required visual or data assets for this AIDA section. 2-4 entries. Each entry names the asset type AND its specific content. Vague entries ('an image', 'a chart') are rejected at intake.

asset_type.description: The kind of asset, e.g. 'UI mockup', 'line chart', 'stat overlay', 'screenshot', 'architecture diagram'.

content.description: What the asset specifically shows. Concrete enough that a teammate could produce it without follow-up questions.

visuals_slides.description: Required visual or data assets for this AIDA section. 2-4 entries. Each entry names the asset type AND its specific content.

judge_calibration_notes.description: Per judge persona, what to emphasize.

fallback_answer.description: One-sentence safe answer for partial-knowledge cases.

vault_update_proposals.description: Structured proposals for Phase 0 infrastructure updates. User reviews and applies manually.

Section_ExternalContextNotes.description: User-maintained free-form Markdown notes section. Never auto-populated by an intake; never auto-stale. The user opens the editor in the PCD Viewer (or the side panel on Grill-Me-eligible Prompt Generator cards) and saves Markdown directly. is_populated flips to true on first non-empty save. The Prompt Generator may inject this section into Grill-Me prompts via the 'if_user_provided' inclusion rule, giving long Grill-Me dialogues durable cross-session memory of past LLM interactions without Startup managing live chat history.

data.description: Free-form Markdown body. User-authored only. Empty string when the section has not yet been populated.
